title: Review: Cell structure; Cell division
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.1.1-c02 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.2-c01 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.1-c12 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.1.3-xt2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: 4.1.1-x01 (written for the game), 4.1.1-q03, 4.1.1-q07, 4.1.1-x03 (written for the game), 4.1.1-q11, 4.1.1-q15, 4.1.2-q02, 4.1.2-q07, 4.1.1-q02, 4.1.1-q05, 4.1.1-x02 (written for the game), 4.1.1-q09. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Prokaryotic cell
items.clue: A cell whose genetic material is not enclosed in a nucleus.

items.label: Chromosome
items.clue: A structure found in the nucleus of a cell, made of a DNA molecule.

items.label: Specialised cell
items.clue: A cell whose structure enables it to carry out a particular function.

items.label: Nerve cell
items.clue: A long, thin neurone that carries electrical impulses around the body

questions.stem: How is the genetic material of an animal cell different from that of a bacterial cell?

options.text: It is a single loop of DNA in the cytoplasm
It is enclosed inside a nucleus
It is found in small rings called plasmids
It is made of protein instead of DNA

questions.explanation: In animal cells the genetic material is enclosed in a nucleus; in bacteria it is a loop not in a nucleus.

questions.stem: A muscle cell contains large numbers of mitochondria. What is the function of these mitochondria?

options.text: To transfer energy by aerobic respiration
To make energy needed for contraction
To join amino acids into new proteins
To store the glucose used in exercise

questions.explanation: Mitochondria are where aerobic respiration takes place, transferring the energy the cell needs. A muscle cell needs a great deal of energy, so its structure includes many mitochondria.

questions.stem: Root hair cells have a long, thin extension that reaches out into the soil. How does this help the cell to carry out its function?

options.text: It makes the cell larger so it can work faster.
It exposes the chloroplasts to more sunlight.
It allows a thicker cellulose wall to form.
It increases the surface area for absorption.

questions.explanation: The structure of the root hair cell relates to its function in the plant: the extension gives a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions from the soil.

questions.stem: A gardener cuts a short piece of stem from a plant. In damp soil it grows roots and becomes a new plant. What does this show?

options.text: Many plant cells keep the ability to differentiate
Plant cells can differentiate only inside a seed
The piece of stem already had hidden root cells
Plant cells grow without needing to differentiate

questions.explanation: Many plant cells can differentiate throughout life, so cells in a cut stem can form new roots.

questions.stem: The image of a cell is 10 mm wide. The real cell is 0.05 mm wide. What is the magnification?
questions.explanation: magnification = size of image / size of real object = 10 mm / 0.05 mm = 200. Both measurements are in the same units, so the magnification has no units.

questions.stem: Why is a Petri dish stored upside down after the agar gel has been inoculated?

options.text: To stop the agar falling out of the dish.
To stop condensation dripping onto the agar.
To keep the culture warm enough to grow.
To hold the lid firmly against the agar.

questions.explanation: With the dish upside down, condensation collects on the lid below the agar gel and cannot drip onto its surface, so the culture stays uncontaminated.

questions.stem: How are the chromosomes normally arranged in a body cell?

options.text: Singly, inside the nucleus of the cell.
In pairs, inside the nucleus of the cell.
In pairs, inside a large gene in the cell.
In pairs, carrying a single gene per pair.

questions.explanation: In body cells the chromosomes are normally found in pairs, and the chromosomes are contained in the nucleus of the cell.

questions.stem: A cut on the arm of a fully grown adult heals as new skin cells are produced. Which statement about the new cells is correct?

options.text: New cells with half the chromosomes are made.
New identical cells are produced by mitosis.
New genetically different cells are produced.
Mitosis has stopped because the adult is grown.

questions.explanation: Cell division by mitosis produces two identical cells and is important in the growth and development of multicellular organisms, which includes producing new skin cells in this context.

questions.stem: A cheek cell is 6 × 10⁻⁵ m wide and a bacterial cell is 2 × 10⁻⁶ m wide. About how many times wider is the cheek cell?

options.text: About 3 times wider
About 300 times wider
About 30 times wider
About 0.03 times wider

questions.explanation: 6 × 10⁻⁵ divided by 2 × 10⁻⁶ is 3 × 10¹, so the cheek cell is about 30 times wider. This is the order of magnitude difference between eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells.

questions.stem: Which statement about plant cells is correct?

options.text: Their cell walls are found in animals too.
Their cell walls are made of cellulose.
Their chloroplasts are in every plant cell.
Their vacuoles are found in animals too.

questions.explanation: Plant and algal cells have a cell wall made of cellulose, which strengthens the cell.

questions.stem: A sperm cell has many mitochondria packed into its middle section. How does this help the cell to carry out its function?

options.text: They carry the genetic information to the egg
They digest a way through the egg's outer layer
They transfer the energy needed for swimming
They make the proteins that build the tail

questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out respiration, transferring the energy the tail needs to swim to the egg.

questions.stem: In a mature animal, what is cell division mainly used for?

options.text: Cell division has stopped in mature animals.
Cell division makes the cells grow larger.
Cell division repairs and replaces cells.
Cell division continues as the animal grows.

questions.explanation: In mature animals, cell division is mainly restricted to repair and replacement.
